faq.q: Is "Hastings" the same as Hastings-Sunrise — and is it in Burnaby?
faq.a: Neither, exactly. Hastings-Sunrise is the City of Vancouver's official local area at the east end of the Hastings Street corridor, and the Paragon name "Hastings" follows that corridor; Burnaby's Hastings area is a separate area in a different municipality, east across Boundary Road.

faq.q: Which schools are located in Hastings-Sunrise?
faq.a: Three VSB elementaries — Dr. A.R. Lord (555 Lillooet Street), Chief Maquinna (2684 East 2nd Avenue) and wək̓ʷan̓əs tə syaqʷəm (3150 Kitchener Street) — and Templeton Secondary, 727 Templeton Drive; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the VSB locator.

faq.q: How does the area connect to downtown and SFU without a SkyTrain station?
faq.a: By the R5 Hastings St RapidBus, which runs from Burrard Station to SFU Exchange with stops at Nanaimo, Renfrew and Kootenay on Hastings Street in the area; routes 14, 16 and 20 also serve Hastings Street, and Kootenay Loop sits at Boundary Road.

Hastings Park is the home of the Pacific National Exhibition (PNE) and Playland, and the City calls the PNE the thing Hastings-Sunrise is best known for; New Brighton Park and its outdoor pool sit on the Burrard Inlet shoreline.

faq.q: What housing forms does the main residential zone allow?
faq.a: The R1-1 District Schedule allows single detached houses (with a secondary suite and a laneway house), duplexes, and multiplexes of up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units, subject to minimum site areas from 306 m² to 557 m² by unit count.
